options: The model learns a set of weights via gradient descent
The model just stores the training data — there's no real training step
The model builds a decision tree from the data
The model computes and stores cluster centroids
questions.correctAnswer: The model just stores the training data — there's no real training step
questions.explanation: KNN is a lazy learner: it does no work until prediction time, when it searches the stored training set for the k nearest neighbors.

questions.questionText: You set k=1 and the model performs great on training data but poorly on new data. What's the most likely explanation?
options: k is too large, causing high bias
k is too small, causing high variance / overfitting to noise
The distance metric must be wrong
questions.correctAnswer: k is too small, causing high variance / overfitting to noise
questions.explanation: With k=1, each prediction depends on a single nearest neighbor, so the model is extremely sensitive to noise and outliers — classic high-variance overfitting.

questions.questionText: Why does feature scaling matter for KNN specifically?
options: It speeds up the (nonexistent) training phase
KNN is purely distance-based, so a large-magnitude feature can dominate the distance calculation
It's only needed for categorical features
questions.correctAnswer: KNN is purely distance-based, so a large-magnitude feature can dominate the distance calculation
questions.explanation: Since KNN classifies by distance, an unscaled feature with a much larger numeric range will dominate the distance calculation regardless of its actual predictive relevance.
